children: rose 2.94% on Tuesday, their biggest intraday percentage gain since May 6, after the country's largest private lender moved ahead with its CEO  succession process, submitting names of two candidates to the Reserve Bank of India.
The bank said on Saturday it had submitted the two candidates without disclosing their names, as it looks to replace CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan, who is due to step down when his term ends on October 26.

The two candidates are HDFC Bank Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha and ICICI Prudential Life Insurance CEO Anup Bagchi, NDTV Profit reported on Monday, citing people familiar with the matter. HDFC Bank did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

CEO succession has been a key investor concern for HDFC Bank since Sashidhar Jagdishan announced on August 29 that he would step down. In July, the bank's board penalised three top ​executives including Jagdishan after judging that employees involved in setting deposit rates for a state agency ​had engaged in "business overreach".

Analysts at Jefferies said the board had moved quickly, adding that an appointment before Jagdishan's term ends could ease investor concerns and limit the impact of leadership uncertainty on business momentum.

The brokerage said investors were comfortable with a leadership change, but felt the appointment should not include former leaders of state-owned banks as that could complicate the transition. Jefferies maintained its "buy" rating and 880-rupee price target.
HDFC Bank shares were up 2.28% at 724.10 rupees apiece as of 9:25 am IST.
